text:
rachael: heads up — last night's long-gen eval had 4 failures that all show `SIGTERM` to the worker around the same wall-clock time window. looks like a clock jump on the runner.

lena: omg, saw that. flaky stacktrace looks like harness kills after timebox expiry. do we still use monotonic timers there?

mike: digging logs now. here's the snippet from runner-12 around the event (timestamps are host time):
```
2026-03-12T04:59:58Z Job started: eval/long-gen
2026-03-12T05:10:03Z Worker pid=2421: generation started
2026-03-12T05:15:34Z chronyd[123]: System clock step detected: -30.21s
2026-03-12T05:15:34Z Harness: timebox expired (wall 300s) -> sending SIGTERM to pid 2421
2026-03-12T05:15:34Z Worker pid=2421: terminated by signal SIGTERM
```
lena: that's suspicious — chrony stepped the clock backward ~30s. if harness used `time.time()` to measure elapsed, the elapsed would jump forward and look like it exceeded the timebox immediately.

tina: reminder: we merged the `use-real-clock-on-timeouts` change in harness two weeks ago (PR #4421). that change replaced `time.monotonic()` with `time.time()` in `harness/timebox.py` to make logs easier.

aj: whoa. that explains it. NTP/chrony adjustments are expected on some infra. the harness should always use monotonic for durations.

mike: repro steps I used locally: run the worker and then force a clock step with chrony: `sudo chronyc makestep` while a long run is in progress. harness killed job immediately as soon as host clock changes.

rachael: confirmed on my local VM too. quick reproduction:
```
# start a long-run harness in one terminal
pytest tests/long_generation.py::test_long_stream --max-time=300
# in another terminal
sudo chronyc -a makestep
# observed: harness reports timebox expired and sends SIGTERM
```
aj: proposed fix: revert PR #4421 change and switch timebox logic back to `time.monotonic()` for elapsed checks. keep `time.time()` for printable timestamps only. add a unit test that simulates a backward jump.

ci-bot: nightly job: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/long-gen/2026-03-12-4599 (attached logs)

lena: short-term mitigation: change the kill behavior to attempt graceful shutdown first — send SIGINT, wait 30s, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after fallback window. that reduces flake impact while we patch timers.

mike: i'm on it. will open a PR that: (1) switches to monotonic in timebox, (2) adds a test that monkeypatches `time.time()` to jump, and (3) updates the kill sequence to SIGINT->SIGTERM->SIGKILL with configurable grace.

rachael: sounds good. can someone add a note to infra to avoid aggressive `makestep` on runners during nightly maintenance? also ask infra to enable `chrony` slewing instead of stepping if possible.

tina: will follow up with infra. FYI we already have a runner image variant with `chrony` configured for slew-only on prod, but some org runners still had step enabled. i'll roll the slew config to the eval fleet.

aj: timeline? can we hotfix today to hedge tomorrow's run?

mike: will draft PR now and flag for urgent review. if reviewers aren't online, i'll revert PR #4421 as emergency rollback and follow with a proper patch.

rachael: thanks everyone. I'll mark the failing nightly as investigational in the dashboard and mute alerts until we deploy the fix.

lena: after fix we should add an e2e harness job that intentionally simulates clock jitter as part of CI so we don't regress again.

mike: PR: https://git.redwood/internal/harness/pulls/4882 (WIP)
